'''David Clayton Lee'''<ref>{{cite web |title=David Clayton Lee () - Basketball Stats, Height, Age |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/players/183424-david-clayton-lee |website=FIBA Basketball |access-date=14 August 2025}}</ref> (born April 29, 1983) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida Gators]] before he was drafted 30th overall by the [[New York Knicks]] in the [[2005 NBA draft]]. He was a 2-time [[NBA All-Star]] and was selected to the [[All-NBA Third Team]] in 2013.

Lee was drafted 30th overall by the [[New York Knicks]] in the [[2005 NBA draft]]. He spent five seasons with the Knicks and in the 2010 offseason, Lee was [[sign and trade|signed and traded]] to the [[Golden State Warriors]]. With the Warriors, he won an [[NBA championship]] in 2015 in his fifth and final season with the team.

After short stints with the [[Boston Celtics]], [[Dallas Mavericks]], and [[San Antonio Spurs]] and becoming a [[free agent]] in June 2017, Lee retired in November 2017.

==Early life==
Lee was born in [[St. Louis]], [[Missouri]]. He attended middle school at [[John Burroughs School]] and high school at [[Chaminade College Preparatory School (Missouri)|Chaminade College Preparatory School]], both in St. Louis suburbs.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Moore |first=Tim |title=David Lee |url=https://www.stlshof.com/david-lee/ |access-date=2023-11-11 |website=St Louis Sports Hall of Fame |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=November 29, 2017 |title=David Lee retires from NBA to become startup investor |url=https://www.bizjournals.com/stlouis/news/2017/11/29/st-louis-native-david-lee-retires-from-nba-to.html |access-date=2023-11-11 |website=St. Louis Business Journal}}</ref> Naturally left-handed, Lee became essentially [[ambidextrous]] when he broke his left arm and learned to play right-handed.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://nba.aolsportsblog.com/2006/12/28/meet-david-lee/ |title=Meet David Lee |work=AOLSportsBlog.com |date=December 28, 2006 |access-date=December 28, 2006 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070403082209/http://nba.aolsportsblog.com/2006/12/28/meet-david-lee/ |archive-date=April 3, 2007 }}</ref> Lee was a [[McDonald's All American]] and won the 2001 Slam Dunk competition.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gatorzone.com/basketball/men/bios.php?year=2004&bio=lee.html |title=David Lee Bio |work=GatorZone.com |access-date=September 16, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150906090540/http://www.gatorzone.com/basketball/men/bios.php?year=2004&bio=lee.html |archive-date=September 6, 2015 }}</ref> Lee was also named a first-team high school All-American by ''[[Parade (magazine)|Parade]]'' magazine.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=1bZQAAAAIBAJ&pg=5066,340251&dq=parade+basketball+all-america&hl=en|title=Meet Parade's All-America boys basketball team|first=Michael|last=O'Shea|work=[[The Portsmouth Daily Times]]|date=April 1, 2001|access-date=September 16, 2015}}</ref>

==College career==
Lee accepted an athletic scholarship to attend the [[University of Florida]] in Gainesville, Florida, where he played for coach [[Billy Donovan]]'s [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida Gators basketball]] team from 2001 to 2005. As a freshman in 2002, he was named to the All-[[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) freshman team by the conference's coaches. During his sophomore season in 2002–03, he averaged 11.5 points and 7 rebounds a game. Lee was named a second-team All-SEC selection in his junior in 2003–04, while averaging 13 points and 7 rebounds per game.

Lee's senior year, he was joined by incoming freshmen and future NBA players [[Al Horford]], [[Corey Brewer]], [[Taurean Green]], and [[Joakim Noah]]. The Gators went on to win the [[2005 SEC men's basketball tournament]]—the Gators' first [[SEC men's basketball tournament]] championship—by defeating the [[2004–05 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Kentucky Wildcats]] 70–53 in the tournament final.

==Professional career==

===New York Knicks (2005–2010)===
Lee was selected by the Knicks with the team's second first-round pick (30th overall) in the [[2005 NBA draft]], following [[Channing Frye]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/history/draft/2005-draft/|title=NBA Draft history: 2005 Draft|work=NBA.com|date=February 27, 2013|access-date=February 28, 2016}}</ref> Lee signed with the team on July 1, 2005.<ref>{{cite web|first=Jon|last=Robinson|url=http://www.ign.com/articles/2006/01/03/david-lee-interview|title=DAVID LEE INTERVIEW|publisher=IGN.com|date=January 3, 2006|access-date=September 16, 2011}}</ref>

[[File:David LeeNYK.jpg|thumb|Lee (right) with the Knicks in January 2007]]
Lee was installed as a starting forward for a stretch of 13 games in December 2005 and January 2006. Lee posted 23 points on 10–11 shooting, along with 15 rebounds and three steals in 52 minutes as the Knicks went on to defeat the [[Phoenix Suns]] in triple-[[overtime (sport)|overtime]] on January 2, 2006. Lee averaged 5.1 points (59.6%) and 4.5 rebounds per game in his rookie season while averaging 16.9 minutes of playing time in 67 games.

After [[Channing Frye]] was injured, Lee started his first game of the season against the [[Chicago Bulls]] on November 28, 2006. On December 16, 2006, he was one of 10 players ejected in the [[Knicks–Nuggets brawl]]. However, he was not involved in the brawl and was not suspended by the NBA. On December 20, 2006, in a double-[[overtime (sport)|overtime]] game against the [[Charlotte Bobcats]] with 0.1 seconds left, Lee scored the winning basket by tipping in an inbound pass. This was within the league's so-called [[Trent Tucker Rule]], whereby a player cannot catch and shoot a successful field goal with less than three-tenths of a second remaining on the clock. At the [[2007 NBA All-Star Game|All-Star break]], Lee had averaged 11.1 points on 61% shooting (first in the league), an 80% free throw percentage, 10.8 rebounds (8th in NBA) and 1.8 assists in 30.9 minutes a game. On February 16, 2007, Lee, playing for the Sophomores, was named the Most Valuable Player in the [[Rookie Challenge]], finishing with 30 points on 14 of 14 shooting from the field and 11 rebounds. On February 23, 2007, in a game against the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], Lee came down on future teammate [[Andrew Bogut]]'s foot and sprained his ankle. The original diagnosis was for him to only miss a few days, but nearly three weeks after the injury he was still unable to play. He was reexamined and the doctor found that he had a much more severe sprain than was originally diagnosed. Lee played only sporadic minutes for the remaining games of the season.

In the 2007–08 season, Lee continued to develop into a major contributor off the bench for the Knicks.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/david_lee/index.html|title=David Lee Stats, Video, Bio, Profile|work=NBA.com|access-date=September 16, 2011}}</ref>

On November 30, 2008, Lee scored 37 points, a career high, and became the first Knicks player with 30 points and 20 rebounds in a game since [[Patrick Ewing]] had 34 points and 25 rebounds on February 23, 1997.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://scores.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=281129018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081201014127/http://scores.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=281129018|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 1, 2008|title=Duhon, Knicks run it up against Jackson-less Warriors|work=ESPN.com|date=November 30, 2008|access-date=September 16, 2011}}</ref>

On December 9, 2008, in a game against the Chicago Bulls, Lee became the eleventh Knick to record 10 consecutive double-doubles.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=281209004|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090106091100/http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=281209004|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 6, 2009|title=Hughes finishes off Knicks with backbreaking 3 in final minute|work=ESPN.com|date=December 10, 2008|access-date=February 28, 2016}}</ref>

Following the 2008-09 season, Lee became a restricted free agent, and would eventually resign with the Knicks on September 24, 2009 on a one-year, $7 million contract after not finding the lucrative $50+ million deal he was searching for. The contract had incentives that could take it up to $8 million if the Knicks were to qualify for the postseason.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nydailynews.com/2009/09/24/david-lee-and-knicks-agree-to-one-year-7-million-deal/|title=David Lee and Knicks agree to one-year, $7 million deal
|date=September 24, 2009 |access-date=June 5, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=4501088|title=Agent: David Lee close to signing with New York Knicks|date=September 24, 2009 |access-date=June 5, 2025}}</ref>

On February 11, 2010, Lee was chosen to replace an injured [[Allen Iverson]] on the [[Eastern Conference (NBA)|East team]] at the [[2010 NBA All-Star Game]]. He became the first Knick to make the All-Star team since [[Allan Houston]] and [[Latrell Sprewell]] appeared in the [[2001 NBA All-Star Game]].<ref>{{cite news|first=Howard|last=Beck|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2010/02/12/sports/basketball/12nba.html|title=Lee, Replacing Iverson, Is Knicks' First All-Star Since 2001|work=[[The New York Times]]|date=February 11, 2010|access-date=February 12, 2010}}</ref> On April 2, Lee recorded the first [[triple-double]] of his career, putting up 37 points, 20 rebounds, and 10 assists against the Golden State Warriors. He became the first player since [[Kareem Abdul-Jabbar]] in 1976 to record at least 35 points, 20 rebounds and 10 assists in a game.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=300402009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100406121953/http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=300402009|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 6, 2010|title=Lee triple-double not enough for Knicks; Warriors' Nelson within 1 of record|work=ESPN.com|date=April 3, 2010|access-date=February 28, 2016}}</ref> At the end of the season, Lee became an unrestricted free agent.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?page=FreeAgents-10-11|title=Free agents: 2010 and 2011|work=ESPN.com|date=June 1, 2011|access-date=September 16, 2011}}</ref> He had recorded career highs in points per game, as well as assists per game.

===Golden State Warriors (2010–2015)===
Lee became an unrestricted free agent in the 2010 off-season. On July 9, he was [[Sign and trade|signed and traded]] to the [[Golden State Warriors]], who sent [[Anthony Randolph]], [[Kelenna Azubuike]], [[Ronny Turiaf]], and a future second-round pick to the Knicks.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors_acquire_david_lee_070910.html|title=Warriors Acquire All-Star Forward/center David Lee From New York Knicks|date=July 9, 2010|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc|access-date=July 9, 2010}}</ref> Lee's contract under the deal paid him about $80 million over 6 years.<ref name="spotrac">{{cite web|url=http://www.spotrac.com/nba/golden-state-warriors/david-lee/ |title=David Lee Contract, Salary Cap Details & Breakdowns |publisher=Spotrac.com |access-date=November 4, 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150706115318/http://www.spotrac.com/nba/golden-state-warriors/david-lee/ |archive-date=July 6, 2015 }}</ref>

In the 2010–11 season, Lee appeared in 73 games (all starts), averaging 16.5 points, 9.8 rebounds, 3.2 assists and 1.01 steals in 36.1 minutes per contest.

On February 7, 2012, Lee recorded his second [[triple-double]], scoring 25 points and getting 11 rebounds, and 10 assists in a loss against the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]]. Over the course of the 2011–12 season, he averaged over 20 points per game, the second such season in his NBA career.[[File:Andrew Bogut and David Lee.jpg|thumb|Lee (right) with [[Andrew Bogut]] in March 2013]]
On January 24, 2013, Lee was named to the [[2013 NBA All-Star Game]] as a reserve representing the [[Western Conference (NBA)|Western Conference]]. He was the Warriors' first All-Star since [[Latrell Sprewell]] in 1997. Lee recorded a career-high 22 rebounds against the Spurs, and recorded his third-ever triple-double against the Charlotte Bobcats with 23 points, 11 rebounds, and 11 assists. Lee finished the season with averages of 18.5 points and 11.2 rebounds per game, and led the league in [[Double (basketball)#Double-double|double-doubles]] with 56. Also, he was named to the All-NBA Third Team.

Lee injured his hip during the fourth quarter of his first playoff game. An [[MRI]] later revealed a "complete tear of his right hip flexor". Lee finished the game with 10 points and 14 rebounds.<ref>{{cite news|first=Scott|last=Howard-Cooper|url=http://hangtime.blogs.nba.com/2013/04/21/david-lee-done-for-the-season/?ls=iref:nbahpt6f|title=David Lee done for the season|work=NBA.com|date=April 21, 2013|access-date=April 21, 2013}}</ref> Despite the injury, which was expected to end his season, Lee returned for the sixth and final game of the series as the Warriors upset the Nuggets. However, the Warriors were defeated by the [[San Antonio Spurs]] in six games in the next round.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/playoffs/2013/story/_/id/9237552/2013-nba-playoffs-david-lee-returns-golden-state-warriors-game-6-vs-denver-nuggets|title=Warriors' David Lee returns|publisher=ESPN|date=May 3, 2013|access-date=May 3, 2013}}</ref>

On February 4, 2014, Lee ended his double-digit scoring streak at 123 games with 8 points in a 91–75 loss to the Charlotte Bobcats.<ref>{{cite web|title=David Lee 2013–14 Game Log|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/l/leeda02/gamelog/2014/|website=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=May 27, 2015}}</ref>

Lee suffered a strained left hamstring in the final game of the 2014 preseason, sidelining him for 24 of the first 25 games of the season. Lee was replaced in the Warriors' starting lineup by [[Draymond Green]], who continued to start even after Lee recovered. The highest-paid player on the Warriors roster at $15 million, Lee became a reserve for the first time since early in his career.<ref>{{cite news |last=Thompson II |first=Marcus |title=Thompson: Golden State Warriors' David Lee has taken one for the team |date=April 3, 2015 |newspaper=San Jose Mercury News |url=http://www.mercurynews.com/marcus-thompson/ci_27846994/thompson-golden-state-warriors-david-lee-has-taken |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150527083341/http://www.mercurynews.com/marcus-thompson/ci_27846994/thompson-golden-state-warriors-david-lee-has-taken |archive-date=May 27, 2015 |url-status=live |access-date=May 27, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Warriors' David Lee adjusts to new role coming off the bench |date=March 17, 2015 |newspaper=USA Today |agency=Associated Press |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/2015/03/17/warriors-david-lee-adjusts-to-new-role-coming-off-the-bench/24918753/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150717222627/http://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/2015/03/17/warriors-david-lee-adjusts-to-new-role-coming-off-the-bench/24918753/ |archive-date=July 17, 2015 |url-status=live |access-date=May 27, 2015}}</ref> On January 27, 2015, he scored a season-high 24 points in a 113–111 overtime loss to the Chicago Bulls.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/id/400578971/gameId/400578971/chicago-bulls-vs-golden-state-warriors|title=Derrick Rose's OT shot lifts Bulls by Warriors; home streak ends at 19|publisher=ESPN|date=January 28, 2015|access-date=January 28, 2015}}</ref> Lee won his first NBA championship with the Warriors when they defeated the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in the [[2015 NBA Finals]] in six games.

===Boston Celtics (2015–2016)===
On July 27, 2015, Lee was traded to the [[Boston Celtics]] in exchange for [[Gerald Wallace]] and [[Chris Babb]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/boston-celtics-acquire-david-lee|title=Boston Celtics Acquire David Lee|work=NBA.com|date=July 27, 2015|access-date=July 27, 2015}}</ref> as Golden State was seeking to offload his salary given his limited role on the team.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Forsberg|first1=Chris|title=Breaking down the David Lee deal|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/boston/celtics/post/_/id/4719793/breaking-down-the-david-lee-deal|publisher=ESPN|date=July 7, 2015|access-date=July 27, 2015}}</ref> He made his debut for the Celtics in the team's season-opener against the Philadelphia 76ers on October 28, recording 8 points and 5 rebounds as a starter in a 112–95 win.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151028/PHIBOS/gameinfo.html|title=Thomas leads Celtics to 112–95 season-opening win over 76ers|work=NBA.com|date=October 28, 2015|access-date=October 28, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151229141100/http://www.nba.com/games/20151028/PHIBOS/gameinfo.html|archive-date=December 29, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> Having entered the season out of shape, Lee started just three games for the team before moving to the bench and eventually out of the rotation entirely.<ref>{{cite news |last1=King |first1=Jay |title=David Lee understands if Boston Celtics fans felt {{sic|frust|ated|nolink=y}} after seeing him play so well for San Antonio Spurs |url=https://www.masslive.com/celtics/2016/11/david_lee_understands_if_bosto.html |work=masslive |date=November 26, 2016 |language=en}}</ref> On February 19, 2016, he was waived by the Celtics.<ref>{{cite news|title=Boston Celtics Waive David Lee|url=http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/boston-celtics-waive-david-lee|access-date=February 19, 2016|work=NBA.com|date=February 19, 2016}}</ref>

===Dallas Mavericks (2016)===
On February 22, 2016, Lee signed with the [[Dallas Mavericks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mavs.com/mavericks-sign-free-agent-david-lee/|title=Mavericks sign free agent David Lee|work=mavs.com|date=February 22, 2016|access-date=February 22, 2016}}</ref> He made his debut for the Mavericks two days later, recording four points and four rebounds off the bench in a loss to the Oklahoma City Thunder.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160224/OKCDAL/gameinfo.html|title=Durant, Westbrook lead Thunder over Mavs 116–103 for sweep|work=NBA.com|date=February 24, 2016|access-date=February 25, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160227105143/http://www.nba.com/games/20160224/OKCDAL/gameinfo.html|archive-date=February 27, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> In his second game for the Mavericks on February 26, he recorded 14 points and 14 rebounds in 25 minutes off the bench in a 122–116 overtime win over the Denver Nuggets.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160226/DENDAL/gameinfo.html|title=Mavericks rally to beat Nuggets 122–116 in overtime|work=NBA.com|date=February 26, 2016|access-date=February 27, 2016}}</ref> On March 25, Lee returned to Oracle Arena for the first time since being traded from the Warriors and got a standing ovation during a [[pre-game ceremony]] in which he received his 2015 [[NBA Championship ring|championship ring]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2016/news/03/26/david-lee-championship-ring.ap/|title=Ex-Warrior David Lee gets championship ring|work=NBA.com|date=March 26, 2016|access-date=March 28, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170118094441/http://www.nba.com/2016/news/03/26/david-lee-championship-ring.ap/|archive-date=January 18, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> Lee missed the Mavericks' first two playoff games against the Oklahoma City Thunder due to a right foot injury.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160421/OKCDAL/gameinfo.html|title=Durant rallies with 34, Thunder top Mavs 131–102, lead 2–1|work=NBA.com|date=April 21, 2016|access-date=April 22, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160422215816/http://www.nba.com/games/20160421/OKCDAL/gameinfo.html|archive-date=April 22, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===San Antonio Spurs (2016–2017)===
On August 2, 2016, Lee signed with the [[San Antonio Spurs]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/spurs/spurs-sign-david-lee|title=Spurs sign David Lee|work=NBA.com|date=August 2, 2016|access-date=August 2, 2016}}</ref> He made his debut for the Spurs in their season opener on October 25, 2016, recording six points, six rebounds, and two assists in 11 minutes off the bench in a 129–100 win over his former team, the [[Golden State Warriors]]. On January 19, 2017, he grabbed a season-high 16 rebounds to go with 10 points in a 118–104 win over the [[Denver Nuggets]]. On March 1, 2017, he scored a season-high 18 points in a 100–99 win over the [[Indiana Pacers]]. A week later, on March 8, he tied his season high with another 18-point effort in a 114–104 win over the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/l/leeda02/gamelog/2017/|title=David Lee 2016–17 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|date=March 17, 2017}}</ref> On June 29, 2017, Lee was reported to have declined his player option, entering the free-agent market.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/article/2017/06/30/2017-contract-options-and-qualifying-offers-guide|title=Guide to 2017 contract options, qualifying offers|work=NBA.com|date=June 30, 2017|access-date=June 30, 2017}}</ref>

On November 19, 2017, Lee announced his retirement.<ref>{{cite news|title=David Lee retires from the NBA after 12 seasons|url=http://www.nba.com/article/2017/11/19/david-lee-retires-nba-after-12-seasons#/|access-date=November 19, 2017|work=NBA.com|date=November 19, 2017}}</ref>

==Television appearances==
In 2007 Lee appeared on the game show ''[[Family Feud]]'', in an NBA Players vs Mothers week, to raise money for charity.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/knicks/news/Lee_Feud.html|title=Lee Stars in Special Edition of Family Feud|work=NBA.com|date=November 13, 2007|access-date=November 13, 2007}}</ref> On April 26, 2009, he appeared on [[Celebrity Apprentice|NBC's ''Celebrity Apprentice'']].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://realitytvmagazine.sheknows.com/2009/04/26/celebrity-apprentice-nba-right-guard-challenge/ |title=Celebrity Apprentice: NBA Right Guard Challenge! |publisher=RealityTVMagazine.SheKnows.com |date=April 26, 2009 |access-date=September 16, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110807094724/http://realitytvmagazine.sheknows.com/2009/04/26/celebrity-apprentice-nba-right-guard-challenge/ |archive-date=August 7, 2011}}</ref> Lee made a cameo in an episode of the now-canceled series ''[[Lipstick Jungle (TV series)|Lipstick Jungle]]'', playing himself. He also made a cameo appearance in the 2009 movie ''[[When in Rome (2010 film)|When in Rome]]''. He also appeared in a segment of the 2009 version of TV series ''[[The Electric Company (2009 TV series)|The Electric Company]]''.

==Personal life==
Lee is a Christian.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jeremy Lin and David Lee – Who Shared a New York City Apartment – Shrimp Fishing in Taiwan Following Basketball Camp|url=http://www.isportstimes.com/articles/3182/20120829/jeremy-lin-david-lee-who-shared-new.htm|work=ISportsTimes.com|date=August 29, 2012|access-date=August 29, 2012|archive-date=August 31, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120831161100/http://www.isportstimes.com/articles/3182/20120829/jeremy-lin-david-lee-who-shared-new.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2009, Lee, along with several other NBA players, joined the Hoops for St. Jude charity program benefiting [[St. Jude Children's Research Hospital]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.cbssports.com/nba/story/13009170/st-jude-utilizes-power-of-love-nba-in-fight-against-cancer |title=St. Jude utilizes power of Love, NBA in fight against cancer |first=Ken |last=Berger |date=March 4, 2010 |access-date=March 20, 2012 |publisher=CBSsports.com |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130902120224/http://www.cbssports.com/nba/story/13009170/st-jude-utilizes-power-of-love-nba-in-fight-against-cancer |archive-date=September 2, 2013 }}</ref>

Lee married Danish tennis player [[Caroline Wozniacki]] in June 2019.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Kimble |first1=Lindsay |title=Tennis Star Caroline Wozniacki Marries David Lee in Italy |url=https://people.com/sports/caroline-wozniacki-david-lee-married/ |website=People.com |access-date=February 1, 2021 |date=June 15, 2019}}</ref> In June 2021, Lee and Wozniacki announced the birth of their daughter Olivia Wozniacki-Lee.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.wtatennis.com/news/2171714/caroline-wozniacki-announces-birth-of-daughter-olivia|title=Caroline Wozniacki announces birth of daughter Olivia|publisher=WTA|date=June 14, 2021|access-date= June 14, 2021}}</ref> Their son James was born in October 2022.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tennis.com/baseline/articles/caroline-wozniacki-and-husband-david-lee-welcome-second-child-james|title=CAROLINE WOZNIACKI AND HUSBAND DAVID LEE WELCOME SECOND CHILD, JAMES |publisher=Tennis.com|language=EN|date=October 27, 2022|access-date=October 28, 2022}}</ref>  Their third child, a boy named Max Wozniacki Lee was born on 26 July 2025.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://nypost.com/2025/07/27/sports/caroline-wozniacki-and-ex-knick-david-lee-welcome-third-baby/|title=Caroline Wozniacki and ex-Knick husband David Lee welcome third baby: 'Couldn't be happier'|publisher=[[New York Post]]|language=EN|date=July 27, 2025|access-date=July 27, 2025}}</ref>
